failures.test: tests/agent-plugin-memos.test.ts > inserting, editing and removing a memo changes only the text and keeps the author and date
failures.reason: expects date null; rhwp 0.9.0 reads and writes a memo's date (ISO, to the second). A person sees a date on each memo. Date round trip proven: apps/host/src/hwp-save-090.test.ts (b)

failures.test: tests/engine-layout.test.ts > vendored rhwp engine puts an inline table below the paper-anchored Square table of the same paragraph
failures.reason: the table geometry passes; its last assertion wants the footnote separator line of a note line whose colour is "none" — 0.9.0 does not draw an invisible line (Hangul does not show it either); body stays above the notes

failures.test: tests/engine-memos.test.ts > editing memos inserts, edits and removes a body memo
failures.reason: expects date null; 0.9.0 fills the date (see agent-plugin-memos)

failures.test: tests/engine-memos.test.ts > reading memos reads the Hancom HWP sample memo
failures.reason: expects date null for a Hancom memo; 0.9.0 reads the date Hangul stored

failures.test: tests/engine-memos.test.ts > memo requests and text reads every JSON escape of the insert request
failures.reason: sends author null; 0.9.0 refuses a memo without an author string (memo_insert_failed). The studio always sends a string (agent-plugin.mjs memoAuthorOf), so nothing a person does reaches it

failures.test: tests/engine-table-resize.test.ts > one cell resize (Shift+arrow) does nothing at the last column
failures.reason: the starting width of a table pasted from HTML is 186.5 px per column on 0.9.0 (189 on 0.8.7, upstream's pasteHtml); the resize steps (+3.7/+3.8 px), the grid, colSpan and the widths after HWP and HWPX save are the same

failures.test: tests/engine-table-resize.test.ts > one cell resize (Shift+arrow) moves the same boundary again and keeps the grid after save
failures.reason: same as above (starting width 186.5 instead of 189 px)

failures.test: tests/section-tails.test.ts > why the lists have to be put back the engine writes a changed section without a master page it read
failures.reason: its own comment: 'when this fails, rhwp keeps the lists itself (edwardkim/rhwp#7899)' — 0.9.0 writes the master pages and memo lists of a changed section itself; the app's put-back adds no second copy: apps/host/src/hwp-save-090.test.ts (a)

failures.test: tests/recovery-main.test.ts > a recovery copy of a file holds what a save would write, in the app data folder, and leaves the file alone
failures.reason: its precondition is the 0.8.7 engine dropping the lists (sectionTailsOf(export) null); 0.9.0 keeps them, the assertion after it is never reached. Covered by hwp-save-090.test.ts (a)

failures.test: tests/recovery-main.test.ts > opening a file with a copy left over corrects against the file, not the copy: lists the copy lacks come back on save
failures.reason: same precondition as above

failures.test: tests/recovery-main.test.ts > opening a file with a copy left over keeps correcting against the file when the restored copy is edited and saved
failures.reason: same precondition as above

failures.test: tests/tab-widths.test.ts > writeTabWidths writes the measures into those tabs, and the engine reads them back (hwp)
failures.reason: the widths are written (its byte assertions pass); 0.9.0 lays a reopened tab out by its own tab-stop arithmetic (2055 HU) instead of the stand-in width 6000 the test writes. The app writes the width the editor measured, so a tab keeps its place: hwp-save-090.test.ts (d)

failures.test: tests/tab-widths.test.ts > writeTabWidths writes the measures into those tabs, and the engine reads them back (hwpx)
failures.reason: same as (hwp)
